coverage.main: Read all seven pages of arXiv 1810.08280v3 (13 April 2019; IEEE S&P Workshops 2019): Sections I-VII, Algorithms 1-2, Table I, Figures 1-3 and references.
coverage.supplement: No appendix or supplement is included or linked. The IEEE workshop version was not retrieved.
coverage.excluded_results: Table I and Figure 3 evaluate append and slack attacks against the model on which they were generated (white-box). Figure 2 is a feature-location analysis.

result_groups.locator: Section V (p. 5) candidate selection; Section V.C 'Attack Transferability' (p. 6)
result_groups.population: 400 random test malware files under 990,000 bytes correctly detected by the source; transfer evaluated on samples that evade the source (EMBER or Full MalConv) and whose original is correctly classified by the other model
result_groups.outcome: evasion of the target detector (malware classified benign)
result_groups.evidence: Section V.C: attacks are evaluated 'on samples that successfully evade the source model and for which the original (pre-attack) sample is correctly classified by the target model'. Both target-clean-correct and source-success restrictions are explicit. Result: 'at most 2/400 samples evade the target model' for each experiment.

f1.evidence: The Full model's accuracy (0.89, AUC 0.97) and Mini model's accuracy (0.73) on the Full test set are reported; for the EMBER model only a previously reported 0.99 AUC on its own test set is cited, not an accuracy.

f2.evidence: Transfer is evaluated only on samples whose originals the target classifies correctly.

f3.evidence: Only samples that successfully evade the source are transferred.

f4.evidence: Counts are given in a literal but bounded form ('at most 2/400') per experiment; the conditioned denominators (source-evading, target-correct samples) and the exact numerators for each attack and direction are not reported.

f5.evidence: Attacks append up to 10,000 bytes or modify slack bytes; the FGM step and slack epsilon are defined in the byte-embedding space (L-infinity and L2 respectively) and mapped back to discrete bytes. There is no input-space L-infinity or L2 radius; the transfer settings (bytes, epsilon) are also not restated. Explicit discrete-binary threat model, not an omitted radius.

f6.evidence: The Full model is trained on a proprietary 12.5M-binary FireEye dataset; no code, model or adversarial samples are linked and a bounded search found none. The EMBER model is public, but the Full model required for either transfer direction is not.

artifact_checks.result: Repository search returned 0 results; the paper links no code. Bounded search.

bounds_checks.reason: The transfer population is target-clean-correct and source-successful by construction; the rate is conditional and no population-level misclassification rate is reported.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. Binary malware evasion is treated as classification misclassification of the malware class.
